text: The subject, Tariq Nawaz, a 36‑year‑old student with a declared monthly income of PKR 25,000, opened his account on 2024‑07‑06 and is rated low risk. Between 2 April and 10 April 2026 the account received a rapid series of inbound IBFT transfers from at least twelve distinct counterparties, each ranging from PKR 16,000 to PKR 84,000. In total, PKR 1,018,000 was credited to the account in less than ten days, with the majority of the funds arriving from different synthetic banks and unrelated individuals. Within the same period the account executed three large outbound wallet transfers to a QuickPay e‑wallet (WLT‑0932): PKR 231,000 on 5 April, PKR 277,000 on 9 April and PKR 134,000 on 10 April, plus a PKR 233,000 cash withdrawal from an ATM on 6 April. The outbound amounts represent more than 60 % of the total inbound value and were moved to a non‑bank wallet and cash in a very short time frame, a classic “mule” pattern. Internal fraud alerts note that two sender banks filed recall requests citing scam complaints, and the outgoing wallet transfers have been placed on hold without any customer contact. The combination of many distinct inbound sources, rapid high‑value outflows to a wallet, and the fraud recall alerts strongly indicate that the account is being used to layer and funnel illicit proceeds. This activity warrants filing a Suspicious Transaction Report.
